Signed by President William H. Taft Tuesday, March 26, 1912

1912 CSR 145

826958Executive Order 1506 — Authorizing Reinstatement of Charles W. Rider as Storekeeper-Gauger in Internal Revenue Service Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1912President of the United States

Mr. J. C. Wilson may be reinstated as storekeeper-gauger in the Internal Revenue Service without regard to the length of time that he has been separated from the service.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

March 26, 1912.

Executive Order 1501 (1912)

by President of the United States
Authorizing Reinstatement of Charles W. Rider in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules

Executive Order 1502

→

sister projects: Wikidata item

Signed by President William H. Taft Saturday, March 23, 1912

1912 CSR 144

826955Executive Order 1501 — Authorizing Reinstatement of Charles W. Rider in Post Office Department Without Regard to Civil Service Rules1912President of the United States

Mr. Charles W. Rider, who resigned from the Department of Commerce and Labor on August 22,1908, may be reinstated in the Post Office Department without regard to the length of his separation or the provisions of the civil-service rules requiring reinstatement in the same department.

Wm. H. Taft.

The White House,

March 23, 1912.
